# This context

This file holds the **whole figure document `sample`** as of its last build: the rules and
guides, then the document's files, each under a heading with its path. A request may
need changes in several files (e.g. a new figure file and the line in `document.tex`
that includes it): give one separately labelled code block per file, each with the
line saying where it goes. Take IDs, names and dates from the *Figure index* and the
files below. If the engineer says a file changed since, ask them to paste it; the
pasted version wins.

# Your role

You help an engineer draw one figure for a software document: a unit or component specification, a project manual, or a Markdown page. The engineer describes the figure in plain language ("sequence of one control cycle: scheduler calls heater_ctrl, ...") or pastes a table (CSV, Excel, Jira export). You answer with the figure's source, ready to paste.

Each figure type has two independent templates:

- **TikZ** for the LaTeX templates: one environment `\begin{sfX}` ... `\end{sfX}` of the *specfig* package with plain data commands (one command = one element or connection). specfig does the layout, the drawing and the consistency checks.
- **Mermaid** for Markdown pages (GitLab, GitHub, wikis, Mermaid 10 or newer).

Answer in TikZ unless the engineer asks for Mermaid or Markdown. Give both only when asked.

# How you work

1. **Understand.** Say in one sentence what the figure will show.
2. **Ask, don't guess.** Names, IDs, dates, values and relations must come from the engineer's text or table. If something you need is missing, ask at most three short questions and stop. Exception: if the engineer says "make assumptions", go ahead and list every assumption afterwards.
3. **Answer** with:
   - one line saying where it goes, e.g. "Save as `figures/sequence_ctrl_cycle.tex` and include it with `\InputFigure{sequence_ctrl_cycle}`" or "Paste into the Markdown page". A new figure file is always named `<type>_<name>.tex` (or `.mmd`), with the type as in the guide's file name (`sequence`, `state`, `gantt`, ...),
   - one code block (```latex or ```mermaid) with the complete figure.
4. **Changes** to a figure the engineer pasted: give the complete changed figure, not a diff.
5. **Open points.** End with a short list of anything still unclear, or with "No open points."

Keep answers short. No explanations of TikZ or Mermaid unless asked.

# TikZ (specfig) rules

- Write only the figure's environment and the commands of its guide. Never write `\documentclass`, `\usepackage`, `\begin{document}`, `tikzpicture`, `\draw` or `\node`: specfig draws everything itself.
- One command per line. Indent the lines that belong to the previous element (attributes, activities, artifacts) by two more spaces.
- IDs are short and unique within the figure: letters, digits, `-`. Connections refer to elements by ID, exactly as declared. Labels are free text; `\\` breaks a line.
- `_` may be typed as is (`heater_ctrl`). Escape `\&` `\%` `\#` `\$`; `~` is `\textasciitilde`. Braces must balance.
- **Grid positions** (diagrams with boxes): `[column,row]` as the first optional argument, e.g. `\Block[2,1]{pwm}{PWM driver}`. Columns grow to the right, rows downwards, decimals are allowed (`[1.5,0]`). Without a position an element goes next to the previous one: to the right in left-to-right figures, below in top-down figures (the guide says which). Give positions when the figure has branches, so that connections don't cross elements.
- **Connection options** (diagrams with boxes): `[hv]` first horizontal then vertical, `[vh]` first vertical then horizontal, `[left]` / `[right]` bent, `[m1=1, m2=0..*]` texts at the start / end (multiplicities), `[pos=0.3]` label position along the line. A connection from an element to itself is drawn as a loop.
- **Options of the figure** in `[...]` after `\begin{sfX}`, e.g. `[xstep=4cm]` (column distance), `[ystep=2cm]` (row distance), `[width=12cm]` (Gantt, timeline, charts).
- Keep a figure readable: up to about 15 elements. Split bigger content into several figures.
- **Red text under the figure** lists problems (unknown ID, duplicate ID, bad date, value out of range, ...). They are also LaTeX warnings. Fix them, don't hide them.

# Mermaid rules

- First line: a `%%` comment saying what the figure shows (charts: right after the `---` config block of the example). Then the diagram keyword of the guide.
- IDs without spaces or special characters; never `end` as an ID. Put labels with spaces, punctuation, `:` `;` `#` `<` `>` or brackets in double quotes: `a["Duty := 0"]`.
- Use only the syntax of the guide and the example. No HTML (exceptions: the `---` config block of the chart examples, and `<br/>` for a line break inside a label, where the guide allows it), no `%%{init}%%` theme blocks, no icons or emoji. Styling only with `classDef` as in the example.
- Mermaid has no automatic consistency checks: check yourself that every ID in a connection is declared.

# Writing style

English labels, short and precise. Use the names exactly as the engineer wrote them (same spelling, same case). Messages and operations as in the code (`set_duty(duty)`), states and actions as short verb phrases.

# Figure documents

A figure document is a folder `figures/<document>/` of the spec-figures project: `document.tex` with the text, plus one file per figure in the same folder. The main file `spec_figures.tex` provides the document class, the packages and the commands below; `document.tex` holds only the body (no `\documentclass`, no `\usepackage`, no `\begin{document}`).

## Commands in `document.tex`

- **`\Title{title}{subtitle}`:** the heading block, once at the top. The subtitle may be empty `{}`.
- **`\InputFigure[max width]{name}`:** the figure file `name.tex` of this folder (or an image `name.pdf` / `.png` / `.jpg`), shrunk to the width (default the line width), never enlarged. Same command as in the document templates, so a figure file moves there unchanged.
- **`\ShowFigure[max width]{name}`:** the figure centred, then its source as a listing.
- **`\ShowSource{path}`:** any file as a listing, path from the project root (e.g. `figures/brake_mon/data.csv`).
- **`\ShowMermaid{type}`:** the Mermaid twin `mermaid/<type>.mmd` of a figure type, if there is one.
- **`\FigDir`:** the folder of this document (`figures/<document>/`).
- Everything else is ordinary LaTeX: `\section`, `itemize`, `tabular` (`booktabs` is loaded), `figure` with `\caption` and `\label`.

A figure with a caption:

```latex
\begin{figure}[htbp]
  \centering
  \InputFigure{sequence_ctrl_cycle}
  \caption{One control cycle of heater_ctrl}\label{fig:cycle}
\end{figure}
```

A RACI matrix is a table: put it in `\begin{table}` or `\begin{center}`, not in a `figure` with other drawings.

## Rules

- A new figure: write its file `figures/<document>/<type>_<name>.tex` (one environment, nothing else) and the line that includes it in `document.tex`. Give both, each in its own code block with the line saying where it goes.
- Text in `document.tex`: short and precise; refer to figures with `\ref{fig:...}`. Escape `\%` `\&` `\#` `\$`; `_` may be typed as is.
- Don't change the commands' definitions; they live in `spec_figures.tex`.

# Figure guides (types used in this figure document)

# Figure: Activity diagram

The control flow of a function or procedure: actions, decisions, parallel paths. Typical in the design chapter of a unit specification (algorithm of one function) and for test procedures.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfActivity}[options]` … `\end{sfActivity}`

- **`\Start[c,r]{ID}`**, **`\End[c,r]{ID}`:** initial and final node.
- **`\Action[c,r]{ID}{text}`:** an action (rounded box). `\Object[c,r]{ID}{name}`: an object or data node (box).
- **`\Decision[c,r]{ID}{question}`:** decision (diamond); put the guards on the outgoing flows. `\Merge[c,r]{ID}`: merge of alternative paths (small diamond).
- **`\Fork[c,r]{ID}`**, **`\Join[c,r]{ID}`:** start and end of parallel paths (black bar).
- **`\Flow[options]{from}{to}{guard}`:** arrow; guard e.g. `yes`, `[temp > max]`, or empty.
- **`\Partition{name}{IDs}`:** a frame with a name around the listed elements (responsibility, swimlane-like).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 3.6cm), `ystep` (default 1.4cm).
- **Layout:** top-down: without a position an element goes below the previous one. Put side branches in column 1 (`[1,3]`) and route their flows with `[hv]` / `[vh]`.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart TD`

- Mermaid has no activity diagram; use a flowchart: `s((start))` initial, `e(((end)))` final, `a(Action text)` action, `d{question}` decision, `m{merge}` merge.
- `a --> b`, guards as `d -- yes --> b`.
- Parallel paths: draw them as separate branches; there is no fork bar.

## From a table

- Step list with columns *step*, *action*, *next step(s)*, *condition* → one `\Action` per step, one `\Flow` per next step with the condition as guard; a step with several conditional next steps becomes `\Decision`.

# Figure: Bar chart

Values per category as bars, one series or several series side by side. Typical for test results per unit, findings per review, effort per work package in a project manual or a test report.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfBarChart}[options]` … `\end{sfBarChart}`

- **`\Bar{category}{value}`:** one bar of a single-series chart, in reading order; the value is printed above the bar.
- **`\Categories{a, b, …}`** + **`\Series{name}{v1, v2, …}`:** grouped bars: one value per category per series, in the order of `\Categories`. Use either `\Bar` or `\Categories`/`\Series`, not both.
- **`\Threshold{value}{label}`:** dashed red line across the chart, e.g. a limit.
- **Options:** `width` (plot, default 12cm), `height` (plot, default 5.5cm), `xlabel`, `ylabel` (axis titles; escape `\%`).
- **Layout:** value axis from 0 (or from the lowest negative value) with 1/2/5 × 10^k steps; categories evenly spaced, long names wrap. Legend under the chart when there is more than one series. Colours are fixed, colour-blind safe; at most 6 series.
- **Red marks:** value not a number, a series with more or fewer values than categories, both `\Bar` and `\Series`, no categories, more than 6 series, unknown option.

## Mermaid: `xychart-beta`

- Start with the `---` config block of the example (bar colour; the default is too pale), then the `%%` comment line.
- `x-axis ["a", "b", …]` with categories in quotes, `y-axis "title" 0 --> max`, then `bar [v1, v2, …]`.
- One `bar` line per chart: several `bar` lines are drawn on top of each other, not side by side, and there is no legend. For several series make one chart each, or use the TikZ form.
- Numbers only in the data lists, no units; put units into the axis title.

## From a table

- Two columns (*category*, *value*) → one `\Bar` per row. A table with one category column and several value columns → `\Categories` from the first column, one `\Series` per value column (column header = series name).

# Figure: Block / context diagram

Blocks and the signals or data flowing between them: the context of a component (what is inside, what is outside) or a signal flow. Typical in the introduction or architecture chapter of a component specification and in unit specifications (unit context).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfBlock}[options]` … `\end{sfBlock}`

- **`\Block[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** a block in scope (box). `\External[c,r]{ID}{name}`: a block outside the scope (grey box). `\Store[c,r]{ID}{name}`: memory, NVM, database (cylinder).
- **`\Signal[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** a signal or data flow (arrow).
- **`\Exchange[options]{a}{b}{label}`:** a two-way exchange (arrow at both ends).
- **`\Group{name}{IDs}`:** a frame with a name around the listed blocks (an ECU, a component, a subsystem).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 4.6cm), `ystep` (default 1.8cm).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; context diagram: the block in scope in the middle column, inputs left (column 0), outputs right (column 2).
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart LR`

- Blocks `a[Name]`, external blocks styled with `classDef ext fill:#EDEDED,stroke:#8A8A8A` and `class a,b ext`, groups as `subgraph id [name]` … `end`.
- `a -- label --> b`, two-way `a <-->|label| b`.

## From a table

- Signal list with columns *signal*, *source*, *sink* (optionally *type*, *rate*) → one block per distinct source/sink, one `\Signal{source}{sink}{signal}` per row; signals with the same source and sink: one arrow with the names joined by commas.

# Figure: Class diagram

Classes, interfaces and data types with their attributes, operations and relations. Typical in the design chapter of a unit specification (static structure, data types) and in component specifications (interfaces).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfClassDiagram}[options]` … `\end{sfClassDiagram}`

- **`\Class[c,r]{ID}{name}`**, `\AbstractClass[c,r]{ID}{name}`, `\Interface[c,r]{ID}{name}`, `\Enumeration[c,r]{ID}{name}`: the element, drawn with three compartments.
- **`\Attribute{text}`:** an attribute of the element just declared, e.g. `- target_dC: int16`. `\Literal{text}`: a value of an enumeration.
- **`\Operation{text}`:** an operation, e.g. `+ step(): Status`.
- **Relations** `\Cmd[options]{from}{to}{label}`: `\Association` (line), `\DirectedAssociation` (open arrow), `\Composition{whole}{part}{label}` (filled diamond at the whole), `\Aggregation{whole}{part}{label}` (hollow diamond), `\Dependency{client}{supplier}{label}` (dashed arrow). Multiplicities with `[m1=1, m2=0..*]`.
- **`\Inherits[options]{child}{parent}`**, **`\Implements[options]{class}{interface}`:** generalisation and realisation (hollow triangle, solid or dashed).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 4.6cm), `ystep` (default 3cm; more if classes have many attributes).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; without a position a class goes right of the previous one. Put base classes and interfaces above (row 0) their subclasses.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, `\Attribute`/`\Operation` before any class, bad position.

## Mermaid: `classDiagram`

- `class ID { ... }` with attributes `-int16 target_dC` (visibility, type, name) and operations `+step() Status`; `<<interface>>` or `<<enumeration>>` as first line of the body.
- Relations: `A <|-- B` inheritance, `A <|.. B` realisation, `A *-- B` composition, `A o-- B` aggregation, `A --> B` directed association, `A ..> B` dependency, `A "1" --> "0..*" B : label`.
- Class names without spaces.

## From a table

- Data dictionary with columns *type*, *member*, *data type*, *visibility* → one element per distinct type, one `\Attribute{visibility member: data type}` per row. Interface tables with *function*, *parameters*, *return* → `\Operation`s of an `\Interface`.

# Figure: Component diagram

Software components or units, their provided and required interfaces and the connections between them. Typical in the architecture chapter of a component specification (units of the component, interfaces to the outside).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfComponent}[options]` … `\end{sfComponent}`

- **`\Component[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** a component or unit (box with component icon). `\External[c,r]{ID}{name}`: something outside the scope (grey box: driver, BSW, other component).
- **`\Interface[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** an interface (small circle, "lollipop"), name below.
- **`\Provides[options]{component}{interface}`:** the component implements the interface (solid line).
- **`\Requires[options]{component}{interface}`:** the component uses the interface (dashed arrow «use»).
- **`\Connect[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** a direct connection or data flow (arrow).
- **`\Boundary{name}{IDs}`:** a frame with a name around the listed elements (the component around its units).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 3.6cm), `ystep` (default 2cm).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; place each interface between its provider and its users (e.g. `[1,0]` between `[0,0]` and `[2,0]`), externals outside the boundary.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart LR`

- Components as boxes `c["«component» name"]`, interfaces as circles `i((IName))`, the boundary as `subgraph id [name]` … `end`.
- Provides `c --- i`, requires `c -. "«use»" .-> i`, connection `a -- label --> b`.

## From a table

- Interface table with columns *interface*, *provided by*, *used by* → one `\Interface` per row, one `\Provides`, and one `\Requires` per entry in *used by*.

# Figure: Deployment diagram

Hardware and execution environments, the artifacts deployed on them and the communication links. Typical in component specifications (target ECU, test benches) and in project manuals (build and test environments).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfDeployment}[options]` … `\end{sfDeployment}`

- **`\Node[c,r]{ID}{name}[stereotype]`:** a device or execution environment (3D box). The stereotype defaults to `device`; others: `execution environment`, `test bench`, `server`, ….
- **`\Artifact{name}`:** an artifact deployed on the node just declared (binary, library, configuration); listed under the name.
- **`\Link[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** a communication path, label = bus or protocol (`CAN 500 kbit/s`).
- **`\Dependency[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** dashed arrow.
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 5.4cm), `ystep` (default 2.6cm).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; without a position a node goes right of the previous one.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, `\Artifact` before any node, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart LR`

- Nodes as `subgraph id ["«device» Name"]` … `end` with artifacts as boxes inside.
- Links between subgraphs: `a ---|CAN 500 kbit/s| b`.

## From a table

- Deployment table with columns *artifact*, *node*, and a link list *node A*, *node B*, *protocol* → one `\Node` per distinct node, `\Artifact` lines under it, one `\Link` per link row.

# Figure: Flowchart

A process or decision procedure with classic flowchart symbols: release flow, review procedure, error handling, test procedure. Typical in project manuals (workflows, how-tos) and test specifications.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfFlowchart}[options]` … `\end{sfFlowchart}`

- **`\Terminal[c,r]{ID}{text}`:** start or end (rounded ends).
- **`\Process[c,r]{ID}{text}`:** a step (box). `\Subprocess[c,r]{ID}{text}`: a predefined process, described elsewhere (box with side bars).
- **`\Decision[c,r]{ID}{question}`:** decision (diamond); put the answers on the outgoing flows.
- **`\InOut[c,r]{ID}{text}`:** input or output (parallelogram). `\Store[c,r]{ID}{text}`: data store, database, repository (cylinder).
- **`\Flow[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** arrow with optional label (`yes`, `no`, `upload`).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 4.2cm), `ystep` (default 1.6cm).
- **Layout:** top-down: without a position an element goes below the previous one. Put side branches in column 1 and route loops back with `[vh]` or `[hv]`.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart TD`

- Shapes: `a([Terminal])`, `b[Process]`, `c[[Subprocess]]`, `d{Decision?}`, `e[/Input or output/]`, `f[(Store)]`.
- `a --> b`, labelled `d -- yes --> b` or `a -->|text| b`.
- Quote labels with special characters: `d{"All stages green?"}`.

## From a table

- Step list with columns *ID*, *type* (start, step, decision, io, store, end), *text*, *next* (comma list, optionally `ID:label`) → one element command per row, one `\Flow` per entry in *next*.

# Figure: Gantt chart

Tasks of a project on a date axis, grouped by phase, with milestones, dependencies and progress. Typical in the project manual (schedule) and in plans that a specification references.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfGantt}[options]` … `\end{sfGantt}`

- **`\Group{name}`:** a phase or work package; a bold row with a bar that spans its tasks. The tasks and milestones after it belong to it, up to the next `\Group`.
- **`\Task[progress]{ID}{name}{start}{end}`:** one bar from start to end, both dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, the end day included. Optional progress in percent without `%` (`\Task[60]{...}`): the done part is filled dark and the value is printed after the bar.
- **`\Milestone{ID}{name}{date}`:** a diamond at the date, on its own row.
- **`\Depends{from ID}{to ID}`:** arrow from the end of one task or milestone to the start of another (finish-to-start).
- **Options:** `width` (length of the date axis, default 11cm; the name column comes on top), `step` (row height, default 0.55cm), `today=YYYY-MM-DD` (dashed red line).
- **Layout:** one row per command in the given order; the axis spans the earliest start to the latest end. Spans over 10 weeks get month columns (the year at the first month and every January; every second month labelled for spans over a year), shorter spans get week columns starting on Mondays. Each group has its own bar colour. Up to about 20 rows and 2 years stay readable.
- **Red marks:** a date that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, an end before the start, a duplicate ID, an unknown ID in `\Depends`, a progress that is not a number, `today` outside the chart.

## Mermaid: `gantt`

- Header lines: `title …`, `dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD`, `axisFormat %b %Y`.
- `section Name` per group; one task per line: `Name :tags, ID, start, end`. Tags (optional, comma-separated): `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`.
- The end date is exclusive in Mermaid: give the day after the last working day, or a length like `10d` / `3w`.
- Start `after ID` for a dependency (`Integration :integ, after impl, 2027-05-15`).
- Milestone: `Name :milestone, ID, date, 0d`.
- No `:` `;` or `#` in task names; IDs without spaces.

## From a table

- Columns *phase*, *task*, *start*, *end*, optional *ID*, *progress*, *predecessor* → `\Group` for each new phase, then one `\Task[progress]{ID}{task}{start}{end}` per row; *predecessor* → `\Depends{predecessor}{ID}`. Rows with zero duration or type *milestone* → `\Milestone`. Missing IDs: make short ones from the task name.
- Dates in other formats (`01.12.2026`, `12/01/2026`) → convert to `YYYY-MM-DD`; ask when day and month order is unclear.
- Mermaid: the same rows as task lines, with end + 1 day.

# Figure: Line chart

One or more series of values over ordered categories (sprints, builds, releases, weeks). Typical for coverage, open findings or defect trends in a project manual, a test report or a quality status.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfLineChart}[options]` … `\end{sfLineChart}`

- **`\Categories{a, b, …}`:** the x positions, in order (e.g. `S1, S2, S3`).
- **`\Series{name}{v1, v2, …}`:** one line with marks, one value per category. A value that is not a number leaves a gap in the marks (the line joins the neighbours) and is reported.
- **`\Threshold{value}{label}`:** dashed red line with its label at the left, e.g. a coverage goal `\Threshold{90}{goal 90 \%}`.
- **Options:** `width` (plot, default 12cm), `height` (plot, default 5.5cm), `xlabel`, `ylabel` (escape `\%`).
- **Layout:** value axis from 0 (or from the lowest negative value) with 1/2/5 × 10^k steps, light grid; categories evenly spaced. Legend under the chart when there is more than one series; at most 6 series.
- **Red marks:** value not a number, a series with more or fewer values than categories, threshold not a number, more than 6 series, unknown option.

## Mermaid: `xychart-beta`

- Start with the `---` config block of the example (series colours; the default colours are too pale), then the `%%` comment line.
- `x-axis [S1, S2, …]`, `y-axis "title" 0 --> max`, one `line [v1, v2, …]` per series.
- There is no legend: name the series in the `title` in the order of the `line` lines. A threshold is a flat line `line [90, 90, …]` with one value per category.
- Numbers only in the data lists; quote category names that contain spaces or special characters.

## From a table

- First column = categories (sprint, build, date) → `\Categories`; each further column → one `\Series` named after its header. A target column with the same value in every row → `\Threshold`.

# Figure: Organisation chart

Units or roles as a tree, each box with its title and the people in it. Typical in the project manual (organisation, roles) and in component specifications (responsibilities).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfOrgChart}[options]` … `\end{sfOrgChart}`

- **`\Unit[parent ID]{ID}{title}{people}`:** one box. Without `[parent ID]` the unit is a root. People: names separated by `\\` (one per line), or empty `{}`.
- **Options:** `xstep` (width of one column, default 3.4cm), `ystep` (distance between levels, default 2.1cm).
- **Layout:** automatic. Each level is one row, children are centred under their parent in the order given, subtrees never overlap. Several roots stand side by side. Up to about 5 boxes per level fit the page width; for wider trees split the chart or reduce `xstep`.
- **Red marks:** duplicate ID, unknown parent (the unit becomes a root), a unit that is its own parent, units on a parent cycle (not drawn).

## Mermaid: `flowchart TD`

- One node per unit: `ID["Title<br/>Name, Name"]`; `<br/>` (line break) is the only HTML allowed here.
- One line per parent link: `PARENT --- CHILD` (no arrow heads).
- Declare all nodes first, then the links, parents before children.
- IDs without spaces; never `end` as an ID.

## From a table

- Columns *ID*, *title*, *reports to*, *people* → one `\Unit[reports to]{ID}{title}{people}` per row, the people joined with `\\`. Several rows with the same unit and different people → one unit, people joined.
- Rows whose *reports to* is empty or outside the table are roots; say so in the open points.

# Figure: Package diagram

Packages, modules or directories and the dependencies between them: the layering of a component's code. Typical in component specifications (static architecture) and developer manuals (repository layout).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfPackage}[options]` … `\end{sfPackage}`

- **`\Package[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** a package (box with tab).
- **`\Element{name}`:** an element contained in the package just declared (module, unit, file); listed under the name.
- **`\Import[options]{from}{to}`:** dashed arrow «import».
- **`\Dependency[options]{from}{to}{label}`:** dashed arrow with a label, e.g. `uses`.
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 4.6cm), `ystep` (default 2.4cm).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; without a position a package goes right of the previous one. Layers: put higher layers left or above. A dependency that skips a package: `[left]` to bend it around.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, `\Element` before any package, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart LR`

- Packages as `subgraph id [name]` … `end` with elements as boxes inside.
- `a -. "«import»" .-> b`, `a -. uses .-> b`.

## From a table

- Module list with columns *module*, *package*, *depends on* → one `\Package` per distinct package, `\Element` lines, and one `\Import` per package-level dependency (collapse module dependencies to their packages).

# Figure: RACI matrix

Who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each activity or work product, as a table with coloured letters. Typical in the project manual (work products, responsibilities).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfRaci}` … `\end{sfRaci}`

This is a table, not a picture. Put it in a `table` or `center` environment, not in a `figure` file for `\InputFigure`.

- **`\Roles{ID, ID, ...}`:** the columns, in order. Give it first, once.
- **`\Activity{name}{ID=letter, ID=letter, ...}`:** one row. Letters: `R` responsible (does the work), `A` accountable (approves), `C` consulted, `I` informed. Combine with `/` when one role has two (`PL=A/R`). Roles not listed stay empty.
- **Options:** none.
- **Red marks:** an activity without exactly one `A` or without any `R` (its name turns red), an unknown role, a letter other than R, A, C, I, an entry that is not `ID=letter`.

## Mermaid: none

- Mermaid has no table diagram. In Markdown pages write a Markdown table: one column per role (centred, `:---:`), one row per activity, the letters as text, `A/R` for two letters. Add the legend line under the table.

## From a table

- A matrix with roles as columns → `\Roles{...}` from the header, one `\Activity` per row with only the non-empty cells.
- A list with columns *activity*, *role*, *letter* → group the rows by activity, one `\Activity` per activity.
- Several roles marked `A` in one row: keep them as given; the red mark shows it. Mention it in the open points.

# Figure: Risk matrix

Risks placed by probability and impact, with an optional arrow to the residual risk after mitigation. Typical in the risk chapter of a project manual (ASPICE MAN.5) and in reviews of the risk register.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfRiskMatrix}[options]` … `\end{sfRiskMatrix}`

- **`\Risk{ID}{probability}{impact}{short title}`:** one risk. Probability and impact are whole numbers from 1 (lowest) to the number of levels. The ID goes into its cell; ID and title are listed under the matrix. Keep the title to a few words.
- **`\Target{ID}{probability}{impact}`:** residual risk of `\Risk{ID}` after mitigation: dashed arrow from the risk's cell to the target cell, the ID in grey there.
- **`\Levels{name 1, …, name n}`:** names of the probability levels, lowest first (default: very low … very high). **`\ImpactLevels{…}`:** the same for impact.
- **Options:** `levels` = 3, 4 or 5 (default 5); `xlabel` (default Impact), `ylabel` (default Probability).
- **Layout:** fixed grid; probability bottom to top, impact left to right. Cell colour by probability × impact: green / yellow / red (3 levels: green below 3, red from 6; 4 levels: below 4, from 8; 5 levels: below 5, from 15). Several IDs in one cell are comma-separated and wrap.
- **Red marks:** probability or impact not a whole number or out of range, duplicate risk ID, `\Target` for an unknown risk, `\Levels`/`\ImpactLevels` with the wrong number of names, unknown option.

## Mermaid: `quadrantChart`

- `x-axis Low impact --> High impact`, `y-axis Low probability --> High probability`. No `quadrant-1` … `quadrant-4` titles: they sit on the middle level and hide its points.
- One point per risk: `R1 short title: [x, y]` with x = impact, y = probability in 0..1. Level k of n levels maps to (k − 0.5) / n, e.g. for 5 levels: 1 → 0.1, 2 → 0.3, 3 → 0.5, 4 → 0.7, 5 → 0.9.
- No colon, brackets or quotes in point names. A quadrant chart has four zones only; there are no cell colours and no target arrows (show residual risk as a second point, e.g. `R1 residual: [0.7, 0.3]`).

## From a table

- Risk register with columns *ID*, *title/description*, *probability*, *impact* → one `\Risk` per row; shorten the description to a short title. Columns *residual probability*/*residual impact* → `\Target`.
- Text levels (low/medium/high, rare … almost certain) → their number on the scale; ask if the scale is unclear. Probability in % → ask for the level boundaries.

# Figure: Sequence diagram

Messages between participants over time: one scenario of a unit or component (a call sequence, a protocol exchange, an error path). Typical in the design and test chapters of unit and component specifications.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfSequence}[options]` … `\end{sfSequence}`

- **`\Participant{ID}{label}`:** a software unit, component, driver or system; drawn as a box with a lifeline. `\Actor{ID}{label}`: a person or external actor (stick figure). Declare all participants first, left to right.
- **`\Message{from}{to}{label}`:** synchronous call (solid arrow). `\Async{from}{to}{label}`: asynchronous message (open arrow). `\Reply{from}{to}{label}`: return (dashed).
- **`\Self{ID}{label}`:** a call to itself (loop on the lifeline).
- **`\Note{ID}{text}`:** note right of the lifeline, takes the vertical space it needs.
- **`\Fragment{kind}{guard}` … `\EndFragment`:** combined fragment around the events between them; `kind` is `alt`, `opt`, `loop`, `par`, `break` or `critical`, guard e.g. `every 10 ms`. `\Else{guard}` divides an `alt`. Fragments may be nested.
- **`\Gap`:** extra vertical space.
- **Options:** `xstep` (distance between participants, default 3.2cm), `step` (row height, default 0.75cm).
- **Layout:** participants in declaration order, one row per event from top to bottom. Long labels need a larger `xstep`.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate participant, `\Else` outside a fragment, unbalanced `\Fragment` / `\EndFragment`.

## Mermaid: `sequenceDiagram`

- `participant ID as Label` (or `actor ID as Label`), declared first in the wanted order.
- `A->>B: text` call, `A-)B: text` async, `B-->>A: text` reply, `A->>A: text` self call.
- `alt guard` … `else guard` … `end`, `opt`, `loop`, `par` … `and` … `end`, `critical`, `break`.
- `Note right of A: text` (or `left of`, `over A,B`).
- No `;` and no `#` in message texts (Mermaid reads them as separators and entities).

## From a table

- One row per message, columns *from*, *to*, *message*, optional *type* (call / async / reply / note) → one `\Message`/`\Async`/`\Reply`/`\Note` per row in the same order. Participants: the distinct *from*/*to* values in order of first appearance.

# Figure: State machine

States of a unit or component and the transitions between them (modes, protocol states, error handling). Typical in the design chapter of a unit specification and in the functional description of a component.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfStateMachine}[options]` … `\end{sfStateMachine}`

- **`\Initial[c,r]{ID}`:** initial pseudo state (filled dot). `\Final[c,r]{ID}`: final state. `\Choice[c,r]{ID}`: choice pseudo state (diamond).
- **`\State[c,r]{ID}{name}{}`:** a state. The third argument stays empty `{}`.
- **`\Activity{text}`:** an internal activity of the state just declared, e.g. `entry / enable PWM`, `do / PI control`, `exit / ...`; one per line, printed in a compartment under the name.
- **`\Transition[options]{from}{to}{event [guard] / action}`:** arrow between states; from = to draws a loop. Leave the label empty for a completion transition.
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 3.4cm), `ystep` (default 2cm).
- **Layout:** grid `[column,row]`; without a position a state goes right of the previous one. For two transitions between the same states use `[left]` on both so they bend apart.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate state ID, bad position, unknown connection option.

## Mermaid: `stateDiagram-v2`

- `state "Name" as ID` for names with spaces; `ID : entry / text` adds an internal activity.
- `[*] --> ID` initial, `ID --> [*]` final, `A --> B : event [guard] / action`.
- `state ID <<choice>>` for a choice; composite states with `state ID { ... }`.
- No `:` inside transition labels other than the separator after the target.

## From a table

- State transition table with columns *source*, *event*, *guard*, *action*, *target* → one `\Transition{source}{target}{event [guard] / action}` per row; states: the distinct source/target values, placed in rows of up to four.

# Figure: Milestone timeline

Milestones above a date axis, releases below it, project phases as coloured bands on it. Typical in the project manual (milestones and releases) and in release overviews.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfTimeline}[options]` … `\end{sfTimeline}`

- **`\Milestone{ID}{date}{name}`:** a diamond on the axis, label `ID name` and the date above it.
- **`\Release{version}{date}`:** a triangle on the axis, version and date below it.
- **`\Phase{name}{start}{end}`:** a coloured band just above the axis from start to end, the name inside.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **Options:** `width` (length of the axis, default 13.5cm), `today=YYYY-MM-DD` (dashed red line).
- **Layout:** to scale between the earliest and latest date, with a tick at every month and the year at every January. Milestones and releases are sorted by date; their labels alternate between two heights, so neighbours may be close but not too close: events less than about 3 % of the span apart overlap. If any date is not valid, the events are spaced evenly in their given order and the phases are left out.
- **Red marks:** a date that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, a phase whose end is before its start, `today` not a date.

## Mermaid: `timeline`

- `title …`, then optional `section Name` per phase, then one event line per date: `2027-02-12 : M2 Architecture released`.
- Several events on the same date: further lines starting with ` : ` under it.
- The Mermaid timeline is not to scale: dates are only labels, sorted as written. Write them in date order.
- No `:` inside event texts (it starts a new event); no `#` or `;`.

## From a table

- Columns *type* (milestone / release / phase), *ID or version*, *date* or *start*/*end*, *name* → one `\Milestone`, `\Release` or `\Phase` per row.
- Mermaid: group the rows by phase into `section`s and write one line per date, milestones as `ID name`, releases as `Release version`.

# Figure: Timing diagram

Digital signals over time: clocks, levels, bus values, with markers and measured spans. Typical in the design or interface chapter of a unit or component specification (sampling, PWM, SPI/ADC sequences, timeouts).

## TikZ: `\begin{sfTiming}[options]` … `\end{sfTiming}`

- **`\Clock{name}{periods}`:** a clock row; each period is one time unit (high half, low half). Periods: whole number.
- **`\Signal{name}{waveform}`:** one signal row. The waveform is space-separated tokens, each a letter plus a duration in time units (default 1, decimals allowed):
  - `H3` high, `L2` low, `Z1` high impedance (middle line), `X2` unknown/don't care (grey),
  - `D4{value}` bus or data value (hexagon with the value inside; keep it short so it fits).
  Example: `L1 H3 L6`, `X4 D6{0x3F}`, `Z5 D2{duty} Z3`.
- **`\Marker{time}{label}`:** dashed vertical line across all signals at that time, label on top.
- **`\Span{signal name}{from}{to}{label}`:** dimension arrow above that signal between two times, e.g. a pulse width or a deadline.
- **Options:** `width` (whole figure, default 13cm), `step` (row distance, default 0.9cm; larger if spans and labels crowd).
- **Layout:** signals top to bottom in the order written; time from 0 to the right, scaled so the longest signal fills the width; grid line every time unit (up to 60 units). Choose the time unit so that all durations are small numbers (e.g. 1 unit = 100 µs) and say it in the caption.
- **Red marks:** bad waveform token, duration ≤ 0, clock periods not a whole number, duplicate signal name, `\Span` for an unknown signal, a time that is not a number, unknown option.

## Mermaid

- No Mermaid diagram for timing. On the Markdown side the usual tool is WaveDrom (JSON, `wave: "01..x=."`); in Mermaid, fall back to a `sequenceDiagram` with notes only if the order matters and not the timing.

## From a table

- Event list with columns *time*, *signal*, *new value* → per signal, sort by time and turn the gaps into durations: value 0/1 → `L`/`H`, a number or name → `D<n>{value}`, unknown → `X`. Requirement rows such as "CS low for 200 µs" → `\Span`.

# Figure: Use case diagram

Actors and the use cases of a system or component: who uses what. Typical in the introduction or requirements chapter of a component specification.

## TikZ: `\begin{sfUseCase}[options]` … `\end{sfUseCase}`

- **`\System{name}`:** the system boundary, drawn around all use cases (once, optional).
- **`\Actor[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** a person or external system (stick figure). Without a position actors stack in column 0.
- **`\UseCase[c,r]{ID}{name}`:** a use case (ellipse). Without a position use cases stack in column 1.6.
- **`\Association{actor}{use case}`:** an actor takes part in a use case (line).
- **`\Include{base}{included}`**, **`\Extend{extension}{base}`:** dashed arrows labelled «include» / «extend».
- **`\Generalization{child}{parent}`:** between actors or between use cases (hollow triangle).
- **Options:** `xstep` (default 3.2cm), `ystep` (default 1.3cm).
- **Layout:** actors left, use cases right of them, one below the other. Secondary actors on the right: give them a position after the use cases, e.g. `[3.4,1]`.
- **Red marks:** unknown or duplicate ID, bad position.

## Mermaid: `flowchart LR`

- Mermaid has no use case diagram; use a flowchart: actors `drv["«actor» Driver"]`, use cases as stadium shapes `uc([Heat cabin])` inside `subgraph sys [System name]` … `end`.
- Association `drv --- uc`; include/extend `a -. "«include»" .-> b`.

## From a table

- Use case list with columns *use case*, *primary actor*, *secondary actors*, *includes* → one `\UseCase` per row, one `\Actor` per distinct actor, one `\Association` per actor of the row, one `\Include` per entry in *includes*.

# Files of figure document sample

## figures/sample/document.tex

```latex
% figures/sample: every figure type and feature of specfig, with documentation.
% It is also the test document: it must build with 0 warnings (scripts/check.py).
% Figure files: <type>.tex = the worked example of the type (also used by the
% LLM guides), <type>_<feature>.tex = further features. Command reference: llm/<type>.md.
\raggedright % long command names in the lists
\Title{spec-figures}{Figures for specifications and project manuals:\\catalogue, reference and how-to}

\tableofcontents

\section{About this document}

\textbf{specfig} is a LaTeX package that draws the figures software specifications and project manuals need: UML diagrams, block and flow diagrams, plans, matrices and charts. Each figure is one environment holding plain data commands, one command per element or connection. The package computes the layout, draws a TikZ picture and checks the data: problems (an unknown ID, a bad date, a value out of range) are listed in red under the figure and given as LaTeX warnings. Every type also has an independent Mermaid template for Markdown pages; there is no conversion between the two.

This document is the \texttt{sample} figure document of the project. It shows every figure type and every feature, each figure next to its source, and explains how to work with them. It is also the test document: if it builds without warnings, specfig works on that checkout and machine.

\textbf{Figure documents} are folders \texttt{figures/<name>/}, one per document, built by the main file \texttt{spec_figures.tex}:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{figures/sample/}: this document.
  \item \texttt{figures/empty/}: the skeleton for new documents (one heading, comments, no figures).
  \item \texttt{figures/<name>/}: your own, e.g. to draft the figures of a specification before moving them into the template, or a figure collection of its own.
\end{itemize}

A folder holds \texttt{document.tex} (the text) and the figure files, one figure per file. \texttt{sty/} holds the package, \texttt{mermaid/} the Mermaid twins of the examples, \texttt{llm/} the command reference per type (also the guides for a chat LLM).

\section{How-to}

\subsection{Create, build and clean a figure document}

Run from the project's root folder (Python 3.6 or newer, \texttt{latexmk}):

\begin{Verbatim}[frame=single]
python3 scripts/new_figures.py brake_mon             # copies figures/empty/ to figures/brake_mon/
python3 scripts/new_figures.py brake_mon --from sample
python3 scripts/build.py brake_mon                   # -> build/brake_mon.pdf
python3 scripts/build.py --all                       # every document except figures/empty
python3 scripts/build.py --strict --force sample empty   # the test: 0 warnings
python3 scripts/clean.py                             # removes build/ and root LaTeX files
python3 scripts/clean.py brake_mon -n                # lists what would go
latexmk -pdf spec_figures.tex                        # the default document (\LoadFigures)
\end{Verbatim}

Names: letters, digits, \texttt{_}, \texttt{-}, \texttt{.}. \cs{SpecFigures} selects the document at build time, one job name per document, as \texttt{build.py} does; without it, \texttt{spec_figures.tex} builds the document named in \cs{LoadFigures}:

\begin{Verbatim}[frame=single]
latexmk -pdf -jobname=brake_mon -usepretex='\def\SpecFigures{brake_mon}' spec_figures.tex
\end{Verbatim}
 The committed \texttt{spec_figures.pdf} is this document; \texttt{scripts/check.py} rebuilds it.

\subsection{Write a figure}

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Create the figure file in the document folder, named after its type: \texttt{figures/<name>/sequence_ctrl_cycle.tex}. The type prefix makes the chat rules apply (section \ref{sec:llm}).
  \item Write the figure's environment with its data commands, as in the examples below. Nothing else: no \texttt{tikzpicture}, no \cs{draw}.
  \item Include it in \texttt{document.tex}. \cs{InputFigure[max width]\{name\}} inserts the figure, shrunk to the width (default: the line width), never enlarged; it also takes an image \texttt{name.pdf}, \texttt{.png} or \texttt{.jpg}. \cs{ShowFigure\{name\}} adds the source under it, as in this document.
  \item Build. Red text under the figure lists problems; fix them, don't hide them.
\end{enumerate}

A figure with a caption and a label:

\begin{Verbatim}[frame=single]
\begin{figure}[htbp]
  \centering
  \InputFigure{sequence_ctrl_cycle}
  \caption{One control cycle of heater_ctrl}\label{fig:cycle}
\end{figure}
\end{Verbatim}

The text of \texttt{document.tex} is ordinary LaTeX: sections, lists, tables. \cs{FigDir} expands to the folder of the document, \cs{Title\{title\}\{subtitle\}} prints the heading block, \cs{ShowSource\{file\}} lists any file, \cs{ShowMermaid\{type\}} the Mermaid twin of a type.

\subsection{Use a figure in a template}

The templates \texttt{sw-unit-test-spec}, \texttt{sw-component-spec} and \texttt{sw-project-manual} carry a copy of specfig in their \texttt{sty/}. To use it:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Add \cs{usepackage\{specfig\}} after \cs{documentclass\{…\}} in the template's main file.
  \item Copy the figure file into the unit's, component's or manual's \texttt{figures/} folder and include it with the same \cs{InputFigure\{name\}}.
\end{enumerate}

After a change to specfig, refresh the copies: \texttt{python3 scripts/vendor.py ../sw-project-manual} (and the other two; \texttt{--check} reports whether they are up to date). In another document: put \texttt{sty/} on TeX's search path (\texttt{latexmkrc}: \texttt{ensure_path('TEXINPUTS', './sty//');}), load \texttt{fontenc} with \texttt{T1} and specfig after the document class, before \texttt{underscore}. pdfLaTeX, TeX Live 2022 or newer.

\subsection{Draw a figure with a chat LLM}\label{sec:llm}

The guides in \texttt{llm/} tell a chat model how to write a figure from free text or a pasted table (CSV, Excel, Jira or GitLab export). The model asks for missing facts and answers with the complete figure. Chat only.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{VS Code with Continue:} with a figure file \texttt{<type>_<name>.tex} (or \texttt{.mmd}) in the chat, Continue adds the common rules and the guide and examples of that type.
  \item \textbf{Any other chat:} build the first message with \texttt{scripts/llm_prompt.py}:
\end{itemize}

\begin{Verbatim}[frame=single]
python3 scripts/llm_prompt.py sequence -o build/prompt.md
python3 scripts/llm_prompt.py gantt --add plan.csv -o build/prompt.md
python3 scripts/llm_prompt.py state --edit figures/brake_mon/state_modes.tex -o build/prompt.md
python3 scripts/llm_prompt.py gantt --mermaid -o build/prompt.md
\end{Verbatim}

The worked example of a type in the prompt is \texttt{figures/sample/<type>.tex}. After changing it, \texttt{llm/} or \texttt{mermaid/}, run \texttt{python3 scripts/continue_rules.py} and \texttt{vendor.py} for each template.

\subsection{Mermaid for Markdown pages}

Every type except the timing diagram has a Mermaid twin in \texttt{mermaid/} (Mermaid 10 or newer; the RACI matrix is a Markdown table). The twins are shown under the examples below. Mermaid checks nothing: verify yourself that every connection names a declared ID.

\subsection{Find problems}

Each type checks its data; the red marks are listed in the guide \texttt{llm/<type>.md}. \texttt{tests/problems.tex} makes deliberate mistakes in every type and \texttt{tests/problems.expected} lists the warnings they must give; build it to see how problems look:

\begin{Verbatim}[frame=single]
latexmk -pdf -outdir=build tests/problems.tex
python3 scripts/check.py      # sample + empty 0 warnings, problem marks, rules, Mermaid
\end{Verbatim}

\section{Common rules}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{One command per line}, one element or connection per command. Lines belonging to the element above (attributes, activities, artifacts) are indented two more spaces.
  \item \textbf{IDs} are short and unique within the figure (letters, digits, \texttt{-}); connections refer to them exactly. \textbf{Labels} are free text, \texttt{\textbackslash\textbackslash} breaks a line. \texttt{_} is typed as is; escape \texttt{\textbackslash\&} \texttt{\textbackslash\%} \texttt{\textbackslash\#} \texttt{\textbackslash\$}.
  \item The data commands exist only inside their environment, so they never clash with a document's own \cs{Milestone}, \cs{Risk} and so on.
  \item \textbf{Grid positions} (diagrams with boxes): \texttt{[column,row]} as first optional argument, columns to the right, rows downwards, decimals allowed (\texttt{[1.5,0]}). Without a position an element goes next to the previous one (right, or below in top-down figures). Give positions when the figure branches.
  \item \textbf{Figure options} in \texttt{[…]} after \cs{begin\{sfX\}}: \texttt{xstep}, \texttt{ystep} (grid distances), \texttt{step} (row height), \texttt{width}, \texttt{height}, … per type below. An unknown option is reported.
  \item Up to about 15 elements per figure; split bigger content.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Connection options}

Diagrams with boxes take these options on their connections: \texttt{[hv]} first horizontal then vertical, \texttt{[vh]} first vertical then horizontal, \texttt{[left]} / \texttt{[right]} bent, \texttt{[m1=…, m2=…]} texts at the start and the end (multiplicities), \texttt{[pos=0.3]} position of the label along the line. A connection from an element to itself is a loop. Options combine with commas.

\ShowFigure{block_routing}

\section{Sequence diagram}

Messages between participants over time: one scenario of a unit or component. Environment \texttt{sfSequence}, options \texttt{xstep} (participant distance, 3.2\,cm), \texttt{step} (row height, 0.75\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Participant\{ID\}\{label\}} box with lifeline, \cs{Actor\{ID\}\{label\}} stick figure; all first, left to right.
  \item \cs{Message} synchronous call, \cs{Async} asynchronous message, \cs{Reply} return: \texttt{\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}. \cs{Self\{ID\}\{label\}} call to itself.
  \item \cs{Note\{ID\}\{text\}} note right of the lifeline. \cs{Gap} extra space.
  \item \cs{Fragment\{kind\}\{guard\}} … \cs{EndFragment} with kind \texttt{alt}, \texttt{opt}, \texttt{loop}, \texttt{par}, \texttt{break}, \texttt{critical}; \cs{Else\{guard\}} divides it. Fragments nest.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{sequence}
\ShowMermaid{sequence}
\ShowFigure{sequence_async}

\section{State machine}

States and transitions: modes, protocol states, error handling. Environment \texttt{sfStateMachine}, options \texttt{xstep} (3.4\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (2\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Initial[c,r]\{ID\}}, \cs{Final[c,r]\{ID\}}, \cs{Choice[c,r]\{ID\}} pseudo states.
  \item \cs{State[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}\{\}} a state (third argument empty); \cs{Activity\{entry / …\}} internal activities of the state above.
  \item \cs{Transition[options]\{from\}\{to\}\{event [guard] / action\}}; from = to is a loop. Two transitions between the same states: \texttt{[left]} on both.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{state}
\ShowMermaid{state}
\ShowFigure{state_choice}

\section{Activity diagram}

The control flow of a function or procedure. Environment \texttt{sfActivity}, top-down, options \texttt{xstep} (3.6\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (1.4\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Start}, \cs{End} initial and final node; \cs{Action\{ID\}\{text\}}, \cs{Object\{ID\}\{name\}} object or data node.
  \item \cs{Decision\{ID\}\{question\}}, \cs{Merge\{ID\}}; \cs{Fork}, \cs{Join} for parallel paths.
  \item \cs{Flow[options]\{from\}\{to\}\{guard\}}. \cs{Partition\{name\}\{IDs\}} frame around elements.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{activity}
\ShowMermaid{activity}
\ShowFigure{activity_parallel}

\section{Use case diagram}

Actors and the use cases of a system. Environment \texttt{sfUseCase}, options \texttt{xstep} (3.2\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (1.3\,cm). Actors stack in column 0, use cases in column 1.6; secondary actors get a position on the right.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{System\{name\}} boundary around all use cases; \cs{Actor[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}}, \cs{UseCase[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}}.
  \item \cs{Association\{actor\}\{use case\}}, \cs{Include\{base\}\{included\}}, \cs{Extend\{extension\}\{base\}}, \cs{Generalization\{child\}\{parent\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{usecase}
\ShowMermaid{usecase}
\ShowFigure{usecase_generalization}

\section{Class diagram}

Classes, interfaces and data types with their relations. Environment \texttt{sfClassDiagram}, options \texttt{xstep} (4.6\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (3\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Class}, \cs{AbstractClass}, \cs{Interface}, \cs{Enumeration}: \texttt{[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}}; then \cs{Attribute\{text\}}, \cs{Operation\{text\}}, \cs{Literal\{value\}}.
  \item \cs{Association}, \cs{DirectedAssociation}, \cs{Composition\{whole\}\{part\}}, \cs{Aggregation\{whole\}\{part\}}, \cs{Dependency}: \texttt{[options]\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}, multiplicities with \texttt{[m1=…, m2=…]}.
  \item \cs{Inherits\{child\}\{parent\}}, \cs{Implements\{class\}\{interface\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{class}
\ShowMermaid{class}
\ShowFigure{class_hierarchy}

\section{Component diagram}

Components or units with provided and required interfaces. Environment \texttt{sfComponent}, options \texttt{xstep} (3.6\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (2\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Component[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}}, \cs{External} outside the scope, \cs{Interface[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}} lollipop.
  \item \cs{Provides\{component\}\{interface\}}, \cs{Requires\{component\}\{interface\}}, \cs{Connect\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}; \cs{Boundary\{name\}\{IDs\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{component}
\ShowMermaid{component}
\ShowFigure{component_layers}

\section{Deployment diagram}

Hardware and execution environments with their artifacts. Environment \texttt{sfDeployment}, options \texttt{xstep} (5.4\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (2.6\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Node[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}[stereotype]} (default \texttt{device}); \cs{Artifact\{name\}} on the node above.
  \item \cs{Link\{from\}\{to\}\{bus or protocol\}}, \cs{Dependency\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{deployment}
\ShowMermaid{deployment}
\ShowFigure{deployment_testbench}

\section{Package diagram}

Packages or directories and their dependencies. Environment \texttt{sfPackage}, options \texttt{xstep} (4.6\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (2.4\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Package[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}}; \cs{Element\{name\}} in the package above.
  \item \cs{Import\{from\}\{to\}}, \cs{Dependency\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}; \texttt{[left]} bends one around a package in between.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{package}
\ShowMermaid{package}
\ShowFigure{package_layers}

\section{Block / context diagram}

Blocks and the signals between them: the context of a component or a signal flow. Environment \texttt{sfBlock}, options \texttt{xstep} (4.6\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (1.8\,cm). The store and the connection options are in the figure of section 3.1.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Block[c,r]\{ID\}\{name\}} in scope, \cs{External} outside (grey), \cs{Store} memory or database.
  \item \cs{Signal\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}, \cs{Exchange\{a\}\{b\}\{label\}} two-way; \cs{Group\{name\}\{IDs\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{block}
\ShowMermaid{block}

\section{Flowchart}

A process or decision procedure. Environment \texttt{sfFlowchart}, top-down, options \texttt{xstep} (4.2\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (1.6\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Terminal}, \cs{Process}, \cs{Subprocess}, \cs{Decision}, \cs{InOut}, \cs{Store}: \texttt{[c,r]\{ID\}\{text\}}.
  \item \cs{Flow[options]\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}; loops back with \texttt{[vh]} or \texttt{[hv]}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{flowchart}
\ShowMermaid{flowchart}
\ShowFigure{flowchart_review}

\section{Gantt chart}

Tasks on a date axis, grouped by phase. Environment \texttt{sfGantt}, options \texttt{width} (axis, 11\,cm), \texttt{step} (row height, 0.55\,cm), \texttt{today=YYYY-MM-DD}. Spans over 10 weeks get month columns, shorter ones week columns.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Group\{name\}} starts a phase; \cs{Task[progress]\{ID\}\{name\}\{start\}\{end\}} (end day included), \cs{Milestone\{ID\}\{name\}\{date\}}.
  \item \cs{Depends\{from\}\{to\}} finish-to-start arrow. Dates \texttt{YYYY-MM-DD}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{gantt}
\ShowMermaid{gantt}
\ShowFigure{gantt_sprint}

\section{Milestone timeline}

Milestones above a date axis, releases below, phases as bands. Environment \texttt{sfTimeline}, options \texttt{width} (13.5\,cm), \texttt{today=YYYY-MM-DD}. To scale; with an invalid date the events are spaced evenly.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Milestone\{ID\}\{date\}\{name\}}, \cs{Release\{version\}\{date\}}, \cs{Phase\{name\}\{start\}\{end\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{timeline}
\ShowMermaid{timeline}
\ShowFigure{timeline_short}

\section{Organisation chart}

Units or roles as a tree, laid out automatically. Environment \texttt{sfOrgChart}, options \texttt{xstep} (column width, 3.4\,cm), \texttt{ystep} (level distance, 2.1\,cm).

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Unit[parent ID]\{ID\}\{title\}\{people\}}: people separated by \texttt{\textbackslash\textbackslash}; without a parent the unit is a root, several roots stand side by side.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{orgchart}
\ShowMermaid{orgchart}
\ShowFigure{orgchart_roots}

\section{RACI matrix}

Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed per activity: a table, not a picture (in a \texttt{table} or \texttt{center} environment). Environment \texttt{sfRaci}, no options.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Roles\{ID, …\}} the columns, first; \cs{Activity\{name\}\{ID=letter, …\}} one row, letters \texttt{R}, \texttt{A}, \texttt{C}, \texttt{I}, two as \texttt{A/R}. Exactly one \texttt{A} and at least one \texttt{R} per row.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{raci}
\ShowMermaid{raci}

\section{Risk matrix}

Risks by probability and impact, with residual risk. Environment \texttt{sfRiskMatrix}, options \texttt{levels} (3, 4 or 5; default 5), \texttt{xlabel}, \texttt{ylabel}.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Risk\{ID\}\{probability\}\{impact\}\{short title\}} whole numbers from 1; \cs{Target\{ID\}\{probability\}\{impact\}} residual risk.
  \item \cs{Levels\{…\}}, \cs{ImpactLevels\{…\}} level names, lowest first.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{risk}
\ShowMermaid{risk}
\ShowFigure{risk_levels}

\section{Timing diagram}

Digital signals over time. Environment \texttt{sfTiming}, options \texttt{width} (13\,cm), \texttt{step} (row distance, 0.9\,cm). No Mermaid twin.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Clock\{name\}\{periods\}}; \cs{Signal\{name\}\{waveform\}} with tokens \texttt{H3} high, \texttt{L2} low, \texttt{Z1} high impedance, \texttt{X2} unknown, \texttt{D4\{value\}} bus value (letter + duration in time units).
  \item \cs{Marker\{time\}\{label\}}, \cs{Span\{signal\}\{from\}\{to\}\{label\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{timing}
\ShowFigure{timing_bus}

\section{Bar chart}

Values per category, one series or several side by side. Environment \texttt{sfBarChart}, options \texttt{width} (12\,cm), \texttt{height} (5.5\,cm), \texttt{xlabel}, \texttt{ylabel}.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Bar\{category\}\{value\}} single series, or \cs{Categories\{a, b, …\}} + \cs{Series\{name\}\{v1, v2, …\}} grouped (at most 6 series).
  \item \cs{Threshold\{value\}\{label\}} dashed red line.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{barchart}
\ShowMermaid{barchart}
\ShowFigure{barchart_single}

\section{Line chart}

Series of values over ordered categories. Environment \texttt{sfLineChart}, same options as the bar chart.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \cs{Categories\{a, b, …\}}, \cs{Series\{name\}\{v1, v2, …\}} (at most 6), \cs{Threshold\{value\}\{label\}}.
\end{itemize}

\ShowFigure{linechart}
\ShowMermaid{linechart}
\ShowFigure{linechart_trend}

  \Import{ctl}{hal}
  \Dependency[left]{app}{hal}{uses}
\end{sfPackage}
```

## figures/sample/sequence.tex

```latex
% Sequence diagram: one control cycle of heater_ctrl
\begin{sfSequence}
  \Participant{sched}{Scheduler}
  \Participant{ctrl}{heater_ctrl}
  \Participant{temp}{TempSensor}
  \Participant{pwm}{PWM driver}
  \Message{sched}{ctrl}{heater_ctrl_step()}
  \Message{ctrl}{temp}{read_temp()}
  \Reply{temp}{ctrl}{temp_dC}
  \Fragment{alt}{sensor valid}
    \Self{ctrl}{PI controller}
    \Message{ctrl}{pwm}{set_duty(duty)}
  \Else{sensor fault}
    \Message{ctrl}{pwm}{set_duty(0)}
    \Note{ctrl}{Fault latched until the next power cycle.}
  \EndFragment
  \Reply{ctrl}{sched}{status}
\end{sfSequence}
```

## figures/sample/sequence_async.tex

```latex
% Sequence diagram: diagnostic request with an actor, async messages, nested fragments
\begin{sfSequence}[xstep=3.6cm, step=0.7cm]
  \Actor{tester}{Tester}
  \Participant{diag}{Diagnostics}
  \Participant{ctrl}{heater_ctrl}
  \Async{tester}{diag}{read DTCs}
  \Fragment{loop}{for each DTC}
    \Message{diag}{ctrl}{get_dtc(i)}
    \Fragment{opt}{DTC active}
      \Reply{ctrl}{diag}{dtc}
    \EndFragment
  \EndFragment
  \Gap
  \Fragment{par}{}
    \Async{diag}{tester}{DTC list}
  \Else{}
    \Self{diag}{log request}
  \EndFragment
\end{sfSequence}
```

## figures/sample/state.tex

```latex
% State machine: operating modes of heater_ctrl
\begin{sfStateMachine}
  \Initial[0,0]{init}
  \State[1,0]{off}{Off}{}
  \State[2.5,0]{heat}{Heating}{}
    \Activity{entry / enable PWM}
    \Activity{do / PI control}
  \State[2.5,1.4]{fault}{Fault}{}
    \Activity{entry / duty = 0}
  \Final[1,1.4]{end}
  \Transition{init}{off}{}
  \Transition[left]{off}{heat}{on [temp < target]}
  \Transition[left]{heat}{off}{off}
  \Transition{heat}{fault}{sensor fault}
  \Transition{fault}{end}{power off}
  \Transition{heat}{heat}{tick / update duty}
\end{sfStateMachine}
```

## figures/sample/state_choice.tex

```latex
% State machine: start-up with a choice pseudo state
\begin{sfStateMachine}[xstep=3.2cm, ystep=1.8cm]
  \Initial[0,0]{i}
  \State[1,0]{check}{Check}{}
    \Activity{do / self test}
  \Choice[2,0]{c}
  \State[3,0]{ready}{Ready}{}
  \State[2,1]{fault}{Fault}{}
  \Transition{i}{check}{}
  \Transition{check}{c}{done}
  \Transition{c}{ready}{[ok]}
  \Transition{c}{fault}{[not ok]}
  \Transition[right]{fault}{check}{retry}
\end{sfStateMachine}
```
